newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt fears airline compensations - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt fears airline compensations - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government is looking to negotiate with local airlines to reduce the amount of compensation the carriers are likely to be awarded in the courts as a result of a government-ordered freeze on air fares between 1986 and 1990, Brazil's leading financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said Tuesday.

Under an out-of-court settlement, the government would offer the airlines compensation that is lower than the amounts sued for or offer to cancel debts they have with the government. In exchange, the airlines would have to withdraw their lawsuits, the paper said.
The courts have already ordered the government to pay Transbrasil 187 million reais ($174.8 million) in compensation for losses incurred by the price freeze, Gazeta said.
Vasp, TAM and national carrier Varig are also suing in the courts.

Varig alone is asking for 3.2 billion reais ($3 billion) in compensation, which would more than pay off its entire debts of $2.5 billion, Gazeta said. ((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
